_about: Phrase banks for places, people and encounters. Picked by data (biome, height, culture type, namebase, zone type) and seeded per place. Invention, provenance new.

phrases: Open water heaves under a wide sky.
Grey swell, and gulls following.
The sea runs in long ridges toward the horizon.
Sand ribs the ground, hot underfoot.
Heat shivers over bare stone.
Thorn scrub clings in the hollows.
Wind scours bare gravel flats.
Frost-cracked stone, and nothing growing.
Thin snow lies in the lee of every rock.
Tall grass, gold and rustling, with lone trees.
Herds have trodden paths through the grass.
Flat-topped trees throw small shadows.
Grass rolls away in every direction.
Larks rise from the grass ahead of you.
The wind combs long grass into waves.
Dry leaves crackle under a broken canopy.
Monkeys argue in the high branches.
Sunlight comes down in shafts between trunks.
Oak and beech close over the way.
Leaf litter muffles every step.
A woodpecker hammers somewhere ahead.
Wet green walls press in on both sides.
Vines hang in curtains; everything drips.
The canopy shuts out the sky; the air is thick and warm.
Frogs shout from every leaf.
Moss furs every trunk and stone.
Ferns stand waist-high under dripping cedars.
Fog hangs between the trees.
Dark spruce stands close and silent.
Needles carpet the ground.
A cold wind moves in the pines.
Low scrub and lichen to the edge of sight.
The ground is soft and cold.
Nothing stands taller than your knee.
Blue ice groans underfoot.
Glare off the ice hurts your eyes.
Crevasses open like mouths.
Reeds stand higher than your head; the ground gives underfoot.
Black water between tussocks of sedge.
Herons lift from the channels as you pass.
The smell of mud and rot hangs low.

time.night: It is dark; you move by feel and starlight.

feature: a nose broken more than once

traditions.Generic: keeps the old customs of the {culture}
traditions.River: lives by the river, as the {culture} always have
traditions.Lake: comes from {culture} lake-folk, who trust still water more than roads
traditions.Nomadic: comes of the wandering {culture}, who never sleep twice in one place
traditions.Highland: comes from the {culture} hill-folk, stubborn and proud

wild.text: A pig-sized lizard crosses your path, considers you, and leaves.
You lose the way for a while among game trails.
A traveller going the other way shares the news from the road ahead.
You find a spring of clean water.

road.text: A carter pulls up beside you. "Going my way? It'll cost you."
A patrol looks you over and lets you pass.
Pilgrims share bread with you at the roadside.

Disease.text: A village by the way has chalked its door with warnings. You go round.

Crusade.text: Soldiers of the crusade stop and question you.

Proselytism.text: A missionary walks beside you for an hour, explaining the truth. You learn a great deal about faith and a little about the road.

Disaster.text: Hungry people at the roadside ask for food.

Flood.text: The way is under water; you wade a long detour.

Rebels.text: Armed figures watch you from a ridge and decide you are not worth the trouble.

marker.text: Signs of something big have been through here: broken branches, a smell.
